A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Time-Aware Auto White Balance in Mobile Photography. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary sections are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original illuminant-estimation experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, a 20-participant preference study, and supplementary raw-to-sRGB experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a cross-camera evaluation on 257 S25 Ultra telephoto scenes in Section B.6 and Table 9.

M1.justification: v1 suggests calibration generically in Section 5. v2 adds concrete transfer procedures: offline mapping of source-camera training data followed by training, and online mapping of target inputs with transformation of predicted illuminants back to the target space. The core architecture, features, and loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section B.6 adds a focused camera-transfer scenario using 257 test scenes captured by the S25 Ultra telephoto camera. The original S24 Ultra dataset, Simple Cube++ evaluation, and supplementary application coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged. The new camera-transfer comparison reuses C4 and C5, both already evaluated in v1, without introducing a new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: The new transfer experiment compares uncalibrated application, offline calibration with training on mapped source data, and online calibration at inference. Section B.6 states that no method had target-camera training examples. Existing experimental splits, training settings, and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section B.6 and Table 9 add a camera-shift analysis testing whether calibration mitigates camera dependence, including an uncalibrated control and two calibration strategies. The previous feature ablations, indoor/outdoor analysis, masking comparisons, and difficult-scene examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model performance. The new Table 9 reports mean angular errors without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports mean angular errors of 2.06° without calibration, 1.70° with offline calibration, and 1.53° with online calibration, alongside C4 at 1.61° and C5 at 1.63°. These are additional transfer results; existing benchmark, ablation, user-study, and raw-to-sRGB results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–10 are unchanged. The calibration extension describes procedures but adds no formal derivation, theorem, proof, or revised mathematical assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: contextual metadata for lightweight illuminant estimation and a 3,224-image dataset with neutral and user-preference targets. The conclusion adds a supplementary-material reference without changing its scientific claims.

C2.justification: v1 already identifies camera dependence and proposes calibration as a mitigation in Section 5. v2 tests that existing proposition without revising the limitation or its explanation. Interpretations concerning contextual cues, indoor/outdoor differences, and difficult scenes are otherwise unchanged.

D1.justification: Section B.6 specifies polynomial mapping of ISO and shutter-speed metadata, a 3×3 color mapping, and the processing order for offline and online transfer. v1 provides only a generic calibration suggestion. Polynomial degree, calibration-fitting data, and fitting procedure remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and central novelty positioning are retained. The added transfer experiment reuses the existing C4 and C5 references; reference reflow and updated page back-references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: Appendix B's existing run-in headings become numbered subsections B.1–B.5, followed by the new B.6. A cross-reference is added to Section 5, with small typographic edits elsewhere. The existing narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the cross-camera Table 9 and relocates the original raw-to-sRGB tables, now Tables 10–11. The existing figures and table designs are retained, with local appendix and reference reflow rather than a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 provides an empirical test of v1's previously untested calibration remedy for camera dependence. Section B.6 and Table 9 compare two transfer strategies against an uncalibrated control and existing baselines, strengthening evidence for practical transfer while preserving the original results. The improvement is limited by evaluation on one target camera and incomplete calibration-fitting details.
